approach: Add a new athena-core module `context_load.rs` that reads existing records only. For each class of work (the job's own class) it takes the closed request jobs and the landed ones among them. Per landed job it sums input + cache_read + cache_write tokens over the job's invocations; output tokens are not "loaded". Per class it reports the mean tokens per landed job, the landed share (landed / closed) and the mistakes attached to those closed jobs. A class with fewer than 3 landed jobs gets no figure. Landed jobs with no recorded token value stay out of the mean and are counted in a note. Mistakes not tied to a printed class's jobs are counted in a "left out" note, never folded in. Wire it as `StatusView.context_load: Option<ContextLoad>` and a `("context", "context_load")` entry in `STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS`. Print it in `display::status` as a `context` header line plus one line per class, shaped like `trend_section`. Set OLY-B-A13-01 in docs/spec.toml to a real mechanism with owner `Athena` and a measure ending `status: context`. Add `crates/athena-core/tests/context_compression.rs`. It writes seeded records as files and loads them through the real loader `Records::load_dir`, then asserts exact figures, the thin-class case, the mistake scoping, equality with `mistake_report`, and the spec entry and gap behavior. For the end-to-end display test, add a test in display.rs's own test module. It commits seeded records in a temp repo, builds an `Athena` with `athena_core::test_support::make_athena`, calls `athena.status()` and asserts on `display::status(&view)`. Also register the new test file in xtask/shard-timings.txt, add a CHANGELOG entry and append decision D175. No drain code, prompt, config or record schema changes.

decisions.choice: Loaded tokens per job = sum over the job's own invocations of input + cache_read + cache_write (Quantity::best_lower, as spent_usd does at store.rs:173). Output tokens are excluded. The class figure is the mean over the class's landed jobs.
decisions.reason: Invocation.tokens (records.rs:729) holds what each call actually loaded, including tool results and turns. The requirement text 'tokens loaded per class of work' (spec.toml:2870) asks for that. A mean over landed jobs is a cost per landed job, the same shape as the planning-cost line.

rejected.why: It is only the estimate of the always-loaded prompt. It misses what is loaded during the turns, so it cannot show compression of what a role actually reads.
Output is generated, not loaded; it would hide a drop in input behind a change in answer length.
With a 3-job floor a median adds little robustness. The mean equals total tokens over landed jobs, which an owner can check by hand.

decisions.choice: Group by the job's class (JobRecords::class, store.rs:165) over closed request jobs (JobState::Closed(_)). Count a mistake for a class only when Intervention.job names one of that class's closed jobs, using Intervention::is_mistake (records.rs:209). All other mistakes go in a 'left out' note.
decisions.reason: Finding 4 needs numerator and denominator over one set of jobs. mistake_report (status.rs:595) groups by the intervention's own class_of_work and counts mistakes that have no job, so it cannot be restricted to a job set without changing its output, which the `mistakes` line and its tests use. It is reused as the cross-check: a test asserts shown mistakes + left out == mistake_report(&records).total.

rejected.option: Call mistake_report().by_class and divide by closed jobs
rejected.why: Its set (all mistakes, by the intervention's class label) differs from the closed-job set; that is the mismatch finding 4 names.

rejected.option: Change mistake_report to take a job set
rejected.why: It would alter the existing `mistakes` line and widen the change.

rejected.option: Fold unattached mistakes into a class by class_of_work

Implement ContextLoad::compute(&Records) -> Option<ContextLoad>. Walk records.request_jobs(); keep jobs with JobState::Closed(_) and a class(). Group by class. For landed jobs, sum input + cache_read + cache_write over job.invocations with best_lower, and leave out a landed job with no token value (count it in landed_without_tokens). Drop any class with fewer than 3 landed jobs and count it in thin_classes. Count a mistake (Intervention::is_mistake) for a class only when its job is one of that class's closed jobs; mistakes_left_out = all mistakes minus those counted for printed classes. Return None when no class remains. Implement lines(): a header line stating the definition, one line per class (`code: 2000 tokens per landed job over 3 landed jobs · landed 3 of 4 closed (75%) · 2 mistakes in those 4 jobs`), and notes for thin classes, jobs without a token record and left-out mistakes, each only when above zero.
